public_rationale: Read with his hedge ('seem to') and in context, the claim concerns AI-native companies like OpenAI and Anthropic, not diversified big tech. It also concerns realized revenue, not run rates. On that reading it holds. Anthropic's S-1 shows $4.6B of 2025 revenue. OpenAI's audited 2025 revenue was reported at about $13B. The next-largest AI-native firm, Cursor, had only just reached a $2B annualized run rate in February 2026, so its realized annual revenue was well below billions. The one material complication is SpaceX's AI segment, about $3.2B in 2025. But that figure bundles X advertising and was disclosed after the post. His doubt about 'how many billions' is opinion and is not scored; both firms did make billions.
limitations: The result depends on excluding diversified big tech (e.g., Microsoft's AI run rate) and counting X advertising as non-AI revenue.
Showing that no other firm had billions rests on searches, not an exhaustive census of private companies.
OpenAI's figure comes from leaked documents, not a public filing.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Only OpenAI and Anthropic appear to make billions in revenue, and the exact amounts are questionable.

statement.excerpt: Even then, only OpenAI and Anthropic seem to be able to make “billions of dollars of revenue,” a statement that I put in quotes because however many billions there might be is up for discussion.

from_speaker: seem to be able to make
however many billions there might be is up for discussion
context: 'all of the companies in question heavily subsidize their products'; 'these are the fastest-growing companies of all time'
our_interpretation: The hedge 'seem to' is kept. The claim is read as being about what public evidence showed at the time, not a guarantee that no other firm exists.

'The companies in question' is read, from the context, as AI-native model and application companies (OpenAI, Anthropic, Cursor, xAI and the like), not diversified big tech (Microsoft, Google), chip makers, or cloud landlords. In the same post he treats hyperscalers separately.
'Billions of dollars of revenue' is read as realized annual revenue of at least $2 billion, not annualized run rates. The speaker himself contrasts run rates with realized revenue.
The 'up for discussion' clause is his skepticism about exact amounts. It is not graded except that OpenAI and Anthropic should in fact have billions.
Period: calendar 2025 (the latest full year) through the post date.
criteria.support_condition: OpenAI and Anthropic each had realized revenue in the billions for 2025, and public evidence by the post date showed no other AI-native company with at least $2B of realized annual revenue (the next largest reporting only run rates).
criteria.contradiction_condition: Credible public evidence available by the post showing another AI-native model or application company with realized annual revenue of at least $2B from AI products, OR evidence that OpenAI or Anthropic did not reach billions.

evidence.excerpt: revenue through the first six months of 2026 was $16.3 billion, far more than the $4.6 billion Anthropic generated in all of 2025.
evidence.locator: entry 'How Anthropic overtook OpenAI to become the AI lab to beat', paragraph 2
evidence.explanation: Anthropic's own SEC filing shows realized revenue of $4.6B in 2025. So Anthropic did make billions, as the claim allows.

evidence.excerpt: OpenAI's reported revenue increased from $3.7 billion (approximately 600 billion yen) in 2024 to $13.07 billion (approximately 2 trillion yen) in 2025. The Financial Times, which also examined the same documents
evidence.explanation: Reports OpenAI's 2025 realized revenue at about $13B, which the Financial Times also examined. Kept as context because the documents were first obtained by the speaker.

evidence.excerpt: The AI coding assistant Cursor has surpassed $2 billion in annualized revenue, according to a Bloomberg source. This individual says the four-year-old startup saw its revenue run rate double over the past three months.
evidence.explanation: The best-known AI-native challenger had only just reached a $2B annualized run rate, after doubling in three months. Its realized revenue over the prior year was therefore well below $2B. This is consistent with the claim, but it is a run rate, so it is context only.

evidence.excerpt: The AI segment (X platform advertising, subscriptions, and xAI compute infrastructure, consolidated through the xAI merger completed in February 2026) adds 17%.
evidence.explanation: SpaceX's AI segment had about $3.2B of 2025 revenue. But that total includes X social-media advertising, and the figure was disclosed after the post. It would challenge the claim only under a broader reading that counts X ads as AI revenue.
